title: Connect a garden hose to its tap with a quick-connect coupler and let it lock
instruction: Connect the garden hose to the tap's quick-connect coupler so that it locks on, then let go of both parts.
context: Anyone who waters a garden, washes a car or fills a paddling pool connects a hose to the outdoor tap with a quick-connect coupler: one hand pulls the sprung collar back and holds it there, the other pushes the brass hose-end fitting in until its flange meets the coupler, and the collar is released so it springs forward and locks. Let go early and the fitting stops short and will not lock; push without pulling the collar back and it will not go in. A hose end resting on the lawn has to be lifted and aligned first, since the hose is anchored at the other end.
setup: Station table; positions in metres, x forward from the arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up; the table top is at z 0.7475. (1) Tap-side female coupler, brass, sRGB (0.80, 0.62, 0.25), fixed to the table, friction 0.3: a square-section body 30 x 30 x 50 mm with a 20 x 20 mm bore 40 mm deep (5 mm walls), mouth toward the robot at world (0.150, 0.000), axis 30 mm above the table (z 0.7775) along +x; behind it a 22 mm diameter, 40 mm long spigot and a 54 x 24 x 15 mm tap stand (coupler total 0.5 kg). A 3.5 x 10 x 10 mm steel pawl (sRGB (0.70, 0.72, 0.75), 5 g, friction 0.2) slides vertically in a slot 4.5 mm wide, 8 mm behind the mouth; its 10 mm height spans 3.5 to 13.5 mm above the axis, so its tip stands 6.5 mm into the bore and reaches the 11 mm groove core wherever the 15.5 mm shaft sits in the 20 mm bore; a 100 N/m spring holds it down (0.15 N), travel 6 mm up. (2) Sprung collar, black anodised aluminium, sRGB (0.12, 0.12, 0.14), 40 g, friction 1.0 / 0.9: a sleeve 44 x 24 x 42 mm over the front of the body (3 mm clear of it all round), mouth flush with the body at rest, sliding 10 mm toward the tap on a 300 N/m spring (1.2 N at rest, 4.2 N at the 10 mm stop). Its 3.5 mm roof is 1.6 mm over the pawl's top (a land that stops the pawl riding up on the shaft) from 4 mm behind the collar's front; the body's top wall is 4 mm thick; in front of that the roof is open, so the pawl can rise only once the collar is 6 mm or more back. Two finger rails, each 20 x 8 x 28 mm, run along its sides (52 mm over both) and end in 2 x 3 x 24 mm thumb ridges at the rear. (3) Hose end, 5 links of 25 mm outer diameter green PVC hose (sRGB (0.10, 0.45, 0.20)), 40 mm long, 12 g each, hinged alternately about the vertical and horizontal axes (0.003 N m/rad springs, light damping), anchored to the table by a 30 x 50 x 25 mm grey steel clamp post at (-0.100, 0.000); the hose lies straight along world yaw -18 deg. (4) Brass male nipple fitting, sRGB (0.80, 0.62, 0.25), 120 g, friction 0.4 / 0.3, at the end of the hose: a 15.5 mm diameter shaft 28 mm long with a rounded nose, a 9 mm wide groove with an 11 mm diameter core 4 to 13 mm behind the flange, a 26 x 26 x 8 mm flange, and a 24 x 24 x 62 mm crimp body with strain-relief boot. It starts lying on the table with its flange face centred at (0.157, -0.083), nose pointing along yaw -18 deg. Locked, the pawl sits in the groove, within 3 mm of a flange at the mouth. To verify the build: a spring scale on the collar's rail reads 1.2 N at the start of travel and 4.2 N at 10 mm; feeler gauges give the 1.6 mm land clearance and the 3 mm sleeve clearance; a depth gauge gives the pawl's 6.5 mm intrusion; the nipple's groove width and core by calliper; the hose's two outer links lift 45 mm by hand against the springs.
scoring: A whole-run record (a linkkit History updated every control step and cleared only by the simulator reset). Measured in the coupler's frame: collar travel c (0 at rest, to 10 mm), flange offset f (mm along the bore from the mouth, negative in front), nipple tilt and sideways offset of the flange centre from the bore axis, and the pawl tip in the nipple's frame. Engaged (the simulation's equivalent of the 10 N pull): the pawl tip centre is 6 to 11 mm behind the flange face (inside the 4 to 13 mm groove) and within 7.0 mm of the shaft axis (core 5.5, shoulder 7.75 mm). Seated: engaged, f between -3.0 and +1.5 mm, tilt at most 12 deg, offset at most 4 mm. Release gate: every pad point of both grippers at least 30 mm from the coupler, collar and fitting, both grippers under 5 mm/s, held 1 s. Ladder: 0 = never seated (engaged) for 0.5 s in a row, whatever the positions; 0.5 = seated for 0.5 s at some time, but at the end not locked with the collar forward (c at most 1 mm); 0.75 = at the end, seated with the collar forward, not yet quiet; 1.0 = that, with the fitting still (under 3 mm/s) and the release gate, together for 1 s. Real trial: a steel rule along the bore (1 mm marks) and a scribed 7 mm line, read in the top video for c and f; a try-square for tilt; video for stillness and the 30 mm clearance; then the 10 N pull, a scored step: a spring scale on the hose just behind the boot pulls 10 N along the bore for 5 s, the fitting must move under 1 mm and stay in; if it comes out the score is 0.5 at most.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Pull the collar back and withdraw the nipple, let the collar spring fully forward (0 mm) and check by feeler that the pawl rests down. Lay the hose straight from the clamp post along yaw -18 deg on a taped outline, the fitting's flange face centred at (0.157, -0.083) with its nose pointing along the same line. The coupler and clamp post are fixed on taped outlines and need no reset.
fidelity: Rigid parts. The ball lock is one steel pawl and a sleeve land (a real coupler has several balls); the bore is square (20 mm) around a round shaft for the rigid-contact solver; the hose is 5 stiff links, 0.20 m long, anchored near the table (a real hose is longer and softer); the collar spring is light (4.2 N at full stroke) to suit the arm's pull.
